title: P0d: baseline snapshots — orchestrator/baseline.py saves the efficiency metrics plus a configuration fingerprint to .orchestrator/baselines/<label>.json, compares two snapshots with the non-inferiority metrics flagged, CLI baseline save|show|compare, README section Efficiency telemetry
spec:
Phase I P0 (brief .orchestrator/phase-i-program.md: preserve baseline so later phases compare Jev off vs shadow vs active, before and after context optimisation, by executor, complexity, task category and review configuration). Base goal/T-0445 after P0c (T-0451: scorecard.efficiency(root, by)) merges.
1. orchestrator/baseline.py: save(label, root=STATE, since=None) -> path writes .orchestrator/baselines/<label>.json (directory created, label validated to [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}) containing: saved_at, window (since/until timestamps and row counts per bucket), efficiency = scorecard.efficiency(root) for by in (None, goal, executor, band, class, role), fingerprint = {pool_toml_sha256, jev: {enabled, mode if present, model, votes, sample}, review: the [review] table (thresholds, tiers, security_paths count), executors: enabled ids with model and complexity range, planner_routes: enabled and tiers, packet_version: spawn's packet header version hash when importable else None, client_version and policy_version as H1 records them, git_head of ROOT, orchestrator package version}. load(label), list_labels(). compare(a, b) -> dict of per-metric deltas (absolute and percent where defined, None-safe) for the primary metrics (tokens and cost per accepted task and goal, tokens to first green, calls and turns per accepted task, amplification) and the non-inferiority metrics (first_pass_rate, fix_round_rate, avg_fix_rounds, gate success share, review request_changes rate where available) each flagged worse/better/equal/undefined, plus the fingerprint diff (which keys changed), so a later phase can state "tokens down X percent, first-pass rate unchanged, fingerprint changed only in jev.mode".
2. CLI: orchestrator baseline save <label> [--since ISO] | show <label> [--json] | list | compare <a> <b> [--json]; text output is a compact table; compare marks worse non-inferiority metrics with an asterisk and a footer line "non-inferior: yes|no|undefined".
3. README.md: new section "Efficiency telemetry (Phase I P0)" documenting the run-row fields (bucket, lineage_root, round_index, band, task_class, executor, model, normalized token fields, usd_source), the lifecycle stamps (created_at, first_green_at, gate_attempts, gate_reds, lineage_fix_rounds, accepted_at), every efficiency metric with its formula, the amplification caveat (observation metric, not a target), the unknown bucket, and the baseline workflow (save phase-h-code before any P1+ change; compare after). Keep it under 80 lines.
Tests tests/test_baseline.py (temp root with synthetic runs and tasks): test_save_writes_metrics_and_fingerprint, test_label_validation_rejects_paths, test_compare_deltas_and_non_inferiority_flags, test_compare_handles_none_metrics, test_fingerprint_diff_lists_changed_keys, test_cli_baseline_save_show_list_compare. Existing tests stay green; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0; git add -A; commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: orchestrator baseline save|show|list|compare work from the CLI and .orchestrator/baselines/<label>.json holds efficiency for all six group-bys plus the fingerprint
README.md has the section Efficiency telemetry (Phase I P0) under 80 lines covering fields, stamps, formulas, the amplification caveat and the baseline workflow
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree
